FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Precious Metals Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division 
Council. 

Platinum group metal wires find extensive use in making thermocouples, resistance thermometers, catalytic 
gauges, electrodes, laboratory apparatus, etc. 

This standard was originally issued in 1973. Subsequently, it was decided by the Sectional Committee to revise 
this standard to bring it in line with international practices and to incorporate the experience gained by the 
manufacturers and users during these years. 

In the present revision, following changes have been incorporated : 

— Three additional sizes namely 0.15,0.75 and 0.80 mm have been added to meet the requirements of the 
industry. 

— The clauses on requirements of purity and finish of the wires have been added. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1 960 * Rules 
for rounding off numerical values (revised)' . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off v^lue 
should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



IS 6683 : 1998 



Indian Standard 

WIRES OF PLATINUM GROUP METALS AND 
THEIR ALLOYS — SPECIFICATION 

( First Revision ) 



1 SCOPE 

This standard lays down diameters, and tolerances for 
wires of platinum and platinum group metals. 

2 STANDARD DIAMETERS 

2.1 The diameters of the wires in mm when measured 
in two mutually perpendicular directions for the same 
cross-section shall be as follows: 

0.05, 0.06, 0.07, 0.08, 0.09, O.IO, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 
0.35, 0.40, 0.45, 0.50, 0.60, 0.70, 0.90, 1 .0, 1 .5 and 2.0. 

2.2 Tolerances on the standard diameters of the wires 
shall be as given in Table 1 . 

Table 1 Tolerances on Diameters of Wires 



Diameter 

mm 

0.05 to 0.09 
0.10 to 0.25 
0.30 to 0.40 
0.45 to l.O 
1.5 to 2.0 



Tolerance 

mm 
±0.003 
±0.005 
±0.008 
±0.01 
±0.02 



3 OVALITY 

The ovality of wire shall not exceed half the 
permissible tolerance on diameter as given below: 

Ovality of wire at any ,, . ,. ,,. ,. 
■^ ^ Major dia - Mmor dia 
cross section = -—^ r 



4 PURITY 

4.1 The combined percentage of platinum group 
metals should not be less than 99.90 percent unless 
specified otherwise. 

5 FINISH 

5.1 The wires shall have smooth, bright and non 
porous fmish. They shall be free from any kinks and 
metal fatigue throughout the entire length and shall not 
have sharp ends. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and 
attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyr^ht 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publication), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue 
of *BIS Handbook* and 'Standards Monthly Additions'. 

This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc: No. MTD 10 ( 3841 ).
